# shop

A Go web service generated by [gobento](https://github.com/Tales-of-zuna/gobento).

## Run

```sh
go run ./cmd/shop
```

The server listens on port 8080; set `PORT` to change it. It connects to the
database named by `DATABASE_URL`, as described in [Database](#database).

Open <http://localhost:8080/> in a browser for the web pages. The HTTP API is
served under `/api`:

```sh
curl localhost:8080/api/health
curl -X POST localhost:8080/api/items -d '{"name":"first"}'
curl localhost:8080/api/items
```

## Test

```sh
go test ./...
```

## Layout

| Directory | Contents |
|---|---|
| `cmd/shop` | Entry point: configuration and wiring |
| `internal/models` | Data types and the interfaces between packages |
| `internal/controllers` | HTTP handlers |
| `internal/database` | Database connection and schema |
| `internal/store` | Data access, implementing the model interfaces |
| `internal/views` | Web pages (the views), served at `/` |

## API

| Request | Response |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/health` | `200` with `{"status":"ok"}` |
| `GET /api/items` | `200` with a JSON array of items, oldest first |
| `POST /api/items` with `{"name":"..."}` | `201` with the created item |

Errors are JSON objects such as `{"error":"name is required"}`:

- `400` when the body is not exactly one JSON object with a non-empty `name`
  (unknown fields and data after the object are rejected);
- `413` when the body is larger than 1 MiB;
- `500` when storage fails. The details are logged, not sent to the client.

## Database

The application stores its data in SQLite, through the pure-Go driver
modernc.org/sqlite, so it builds without a C compiler. `DATABASE_URL` is the
database file path or a modernc.org/sqlite connection string; by default it is
`shop.db` in the working directory (`DefaultURL` in
`internal/database`).

Tests need no setup: `internal/database/dbtest` gives every test an
empty database file of its own in a temporary directory.

### Schema

`internal/database/schema.sql` is embedded in the binary and applied
every time the application starts. It uses `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, so it
creates missing tables but never changes existing ones: it is not a migration
system. Before you change the schema of a database that already holds data,
add a migration tool or change the existing tables by hand.

## Changing queries

Data access is generated by [sqlc](https://docs.sqlc.dev/) from
`internal/store/queries.sql` and the schema in
`internal/database/schema.sql`, with sqlc's
`sqlite` engine, so write queries in that SQL dialect;
`sqlc.arg(name)` declares a parameter in any dialect. The generated code in
`internal/store/sqlcgen` is committed; do not edit it by hand. After
changing the schema or the queries, regenerate it with `make generate`, or
without make:

```sh
go run github.com/sqlc-dev/sqlc/cmd/sqlc@v1.31.1 generate
```

The CI workflow runs `sqlc diff` and fails when the committed code is not
what sqlc generates from the queries and the schema.

## Web pages

The pages are rendered on the server from [templ](https://templ.guide)
components and made interactive with [htmx](https://htmx.org). Open
<http://localhost:8080/> after `go run ./cmd/shop`: the form adds an
item without reloading the page, and still works with JavaScript turned off.

| Request | Response |
|---|---|
| `GET /` | `200` with the page listing every item and a form |
| `POST /items` with the form field `name` | `303` to `/`, or for htmx `200` with the new item |
| `GET /static/...` | The stylesheet and htmx, embedded in the binary |

A blank name is answered with `422` and a message next to the field. Unsafe
requests from other sites, such as a form elsewhere that posts here, get
`403`. Every path outside `/api/` belongs to the pages; the JSON API is
under `/api/`.

### Changing the pages

The components live in `internal/views/pages.templ`. The Go code templ
generates from it, `pages_templ.go`, is committed, so the project builds
without the templ command. After editing `pages.templ`, regenerate it with
templ v0.3.1100, the version in `go.mod`, using
`make generate`, or without make:

```sh
go generate ./internal/views
```

The `//go:generate` line in `internal/views/handler.go` runs
`go run github.com/a-h/templ/cmd/templ@v0.3.1100 generate`.
The CI workflow runs it too and fails when the committed `pages_templ.go` is
not what templ generates from `pages.templ`.

htmx 2.0.11 is in `internal/views/static/htmx.min.js`, and the
styles are plain CSS in `internal/views/static/styles.css`. To update htmx,
replace the file with `dist/htmx.min.js` of a newer release.

## Development

`make` lists the tasks of the `Makefile`. Each one runs plain `go` or
`docker` commands, so without make (for example on Windows) run the command
next to it instead:

| Task | With make | Without make |
|---|---|---|
| Build the binary into `bin/` | `make build` | `go build -o bin/shop ./cmd/shop` |
| Run the server | `make run` | `go run ./cmd/shop` |
| Run the tests | `make test` | `go test ./...` |
| Run the tests with coverage | `make cover` | `go test -coverprofile=coverage.out ./...` |
| Vet the code | `make vet` | `go vet ./...` |
| Lint and check formatting | `make lint` | `go run github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/v2/cmd/golangci-lint@v2.15.0 run` |
| Format the code | `make fmt` | `go run github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/v2/cmd/golangci-lint@v2.15.0 fmt` |
| Tidy `go.mod` and `go.sum` | `make tidy` | `go mod tidy` |
| Run vet, lint, and the tests | `make check` | the three commands above |
| Build the container image | `make docker-build` | `docker build --tag shop .` |
| Run the container image | `make docker-run` | `docker run --rm --publish 8080:8080 shop` |

On Windows, `go build` needs `-o bin/shop.exe`; `make build` adds the
`.exe` itself. The linter's configuration is in `.golangci.yml`.

### Docker

The `Dockerfile` builds a static binary with cgo disabled and copies it into
a distroless image, which has no shell or package manager and runs the
server as the non-root user 65532 on port 8080. Building needs BuildKit, the
default builder of Docker 23 and later. The image reads `PORT` and
`DATABASE_URL` like the binary; `make docker-run DATABASE_URL=...` passes a
connection string to it.

In the image, the SQLite database is `/data/shop.db` (`DATABASE_URL`), in
a volume at `/data` that the non-root user can write. Without a named volume,
Docker creates an anonymous one, and `docker run --rm` deletes it with the
container. `make docker-run` keeps the data in the named volume
`shop-data`; without make:

```sh
docker run --rm --publish 8080:8080 --volume shop-data:/data shop
```

To use a directory of the host instead (`--volume "$PWD/data:/data"`), make
it writable for the user 65532, for example with `--user "$(id -u)"`.

The pages and their static files are compiled into the binary, so the image
needs nothing else to serve them: the pages are at `/`, and the JSON API, its
health check included, is under `/api/` (`/api/health`).

### Continuous integration

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on every pull request and every push to
`main`. It checks that `go.mod` and `go.sum` are tidy, builds, vets, lints,
and runs the tests with the race detector, and it builds the container
image. Its actions are pinned by commit SHA, and the runtime image by
digest; `.github/dependabot.yml` keeps them, and the Go modules, up to date.
